title: Age, rules and real platforms
hook: You are 14 and want to try a real crypto app. It asks for your date of birth and a photo of your ID. A friend says: "Just use your mum's account."
card1: Most real crypto platforms, called an [[exchange]], only accept adults (18+). Before you can buy anything, they check who you are. This is called [[kyc]].
analogy1: An identity check is like showing ID at a bank or for a phone contract. It's a bit annoying, but it makes it harder for criminals to hide stolen money.
card2: Using someone else's account breaks the platform's rules. The account can be frozen with the money inside, and the owner is responsible for everything done with it.
card3: In many countries, including Estonia and Finland, profits from crypto can be taxed. That's one more reason to do it openly, with an adult who knows the rules.

account.prompt: A friend says: "Not 18 yet? Just open an account with your mum's ID. She won't notice."

borrow.label: Use your mum's ID without asking
borrow.before: You will sign up with your mum's details.
borrow.what: The platform noticed unusual activity and froze the account. Your mum got an email about it, and the money was stuck.
borrow.why: An account belongs to the person whose ID was used. Using someone's ID without permission breaks the rules and their trust.
borrow.how: Platforms watch for signs that the owner isn't the one using the account, and can freeze it.
borrow.realLife: Never use someone else's identity, not even family. It can cause real trouble for both of you.

noCheck.label: Find an app that doesn't ask your age
noCheck.before: You will look for a platform with no checks.
noCheck.what: You found one, but it had no licence, no support and terrible reviews. The practice coins you put in couldn't be taken out.
noCheck.why: Platforms that skip checks often skip other rules too, like keeping your money safe.
noCheck.how: Licensed platforms in the EU must follow rules, including checking identity. Ones that don't are risky.
noCheck.realLife: No ID check is a warning sign, not a feature.

talk.label: Talk to a parent and keep practising here
talk.before: You will tell a parent what you want to try.
talk.what: Your parent was glad you asked. You agreed to keep learning with practice coins and look at it together when you're older.
talk.why: An adult can help you understand the rules, and you avoid breaking them.
talk.how: Learning with practice coins first means you already know the traps when you start for real.
talk.realLife: When the time comes, start with an adult, a licensed platform and only a small amount.

q1.prompt: Why do real exchanges ask for your ID?
q1.a: To check who you are and make crime harder
q1.c: They don't have to: it's optional if you ask nicely
q1.explanation: Licensed platforms in many countries, including the EU, must check identity to fight money laundering and fraud.

q2.prompt: You are under 18 and want to use a real exchange. What is the right move?
q2.a: Use a parent's ID and be careful
q2.b: Talk to a parent, learn with practice coins and wait until you're allowed
q2.c: Find an app with no age check
q2.explanation: Most exchanges are for adults. Learning first with practice coins and an adult you trust is the safe way.

q3.b: Only when you change coins back into euros
q3.c: Yes, in many countries, including Estonia and Finland
q3.explanation: Tax rules differ by country, but crypto profits are often taxed. That's one more reason to do it openly with an adult.

misc.sellData: "They only want to sell my data." Identity checks are required by law in many countries, to fight crime and fraud.
misc.optional: "ID checks are optional." Licensed platforms must check identity. Ones that don't are a warning sign.
misc.parentId: "Using a parent's ID is fine if I'm careful." It breaks the rules, and the account can be frozen and the owner held responsible.
misc.noCheckApp: "An app with no age check is a good option." No checks usually means no protection for you either.
misc.taxFree: "Crypto is tax-free." In many countries, including Estonia and Finland, crypto profits can be taxed.
misc.onlyCash: "Tax only matters when I cash out to euros." Rules differ by country, and swapping one coin for another can count too.

t1: Most real exchanges are for adults (18+) and check your ID.
t2: Never use someone else's account or ID, not even family.
t3: Crypto profits can be taxed. When the time comes, start with an adult and a licensed platform.
talk1: What rules does our family want for money apps and online payments?
talk2: When you are old enough, how would you like to take the first step, and who would you ask?
